- When sentiment is positive (≥0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% below peak for 3–7 days.  
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.2) over 3+ days, model underestimates; add 3–7% to forecast for next 5–10 days.  
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if price is above 30-day moving average, forecast should be adjusted downward by 1–3% per day until convergence.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture early downward momentum; if true outcome drops >5% from prior day, adjust forecast down by 1–2% for next 3 days.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.00, 1.00, 0.00), model tends to lag; add 1–3% to forecast for next 2–5 days to catch momentum.
